protocol.name: treeland_output_mirror_manager_unstable_v1
protocol.copyright: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2024 - 2026 UnionTech Software Technology Co., Ltd. SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
protocol.description:
This protocol lets a privileged client such as the DDE display settings panel organize physical outputs into mirroring groups: one source output whose rendered content is duplicated to one or more mirror outputs, so that several screens show the same desktop. This is the "copy mode" of the compositor, as opposed to the default "extension" mode where each output shows an independent desktop region.
The protocol exposes a singleton manager global that creates and tracks treeland_output_mirror_group_v1 objects. Each group designates a single source output and an ordered list of mirror outputs, all referenced by their wl_output objects. An output may belong to at most one group at a time. A group drives copy mode while it has both a source and at least one mirror; a group with no source or no mirrors is inert and the affected outputs behave as normal extension outputs.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.

interface.name: treeland_output_mirror_manager_v1
interface.description:
A singleton global that creates treeland_output_mirror_group_v1 objects and broadcasts the set of existing groups to bound clients.
When a client binds this interface, the compositor immediately emits one group_added event for each group that already exists, handing the client a live group object for each of them. When any client creates a new group, every other bound client receives a group_added event for it; when a group is dissolved, every bound client receives a group_removed event. Clients therefore never need to poll for the group set and must not assume it stays consistent between events.
The protocol is intended for a single privileged client such as the DDE display settings panel. Multiple clients may bind concurrently for observation, but only one client is expected to drive configuration; concurrent conflicting edits from several clients are not supported and may fail with fatal protocol errors.

enum.name: error
enum.description: Raised as fatal protocol errors on the manager object.

entry.name: invalid_name
entry.summary: the group name is empty, not valid UTF-8, contains a NUL byte, or is rejected by the compositor

entry.name: name_exists
entry.summary: a group with the requested name already exists

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the treeland_output_mirror_manager_v1 object and release the client's binding to the manager global.
Existing treeland_output_mirror_group_v1 objects are not affected and remain valid until they are destroyed or the compositor dissolves the group. The client must destroy each group object separately; the compositor does not cascade destruction from the manager.

request.name: create_group

description.summary: create a new output mirror group

request.description:
Create a new, initially empty treeland_output_mirror_group_v1 object. The new group has no source and no mirrors; the client configures it afterwards with set_source and add_output on the returned object. Copy mode engages once the group has both a source and at least one mirror.
The name identifies the group in group_added and group_removed events and must be unique among existing groups. It must be a non-empty UTF-8 string and must not contain a NUL byte. The compositor may reject names it considers too long with the invalid_name error. An empty name, a name that is not valid UTF-8, or a name containing a NUL byte is rejected with the invalid_name error. A name that already identifies an existing group is rejected with the name_exists error.
These name checks are deterministic at request time, so the compositor raises them as fatal protocol errors on the manager object and does not create the group object.
On success the compositor broadcasts a group_added event carrying a new group object to every other bound client; the calling client receives its group object only as the new_id return value of this request and does not receive a group_added event for it.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: unique UTF-8 name for the group

event.name: group_added
event.description:
Emitted when a mirror group is created by any client. Each bound client receives this event once per existing group immediately after binding the manager, and again whenever a new group is created, except for the client that created the group, which receives the group object as the new_id return value of create_group instead.
The id argument is a fresh treeland_output_mirror_group_v1 object bound to the group; the compositor sends the initial source and output_added state of the group on it immediately after this event. The client may destroy the object if it does not need to observe or drive that group; doing so does not dissolve the group.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: a group object bound to the new group

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the name of the new group

event.name: group_removed
event.description: Emitted when a mirror group is dissolved, whether because a client sent the dissolve request or because the compositor removed it as a whole. Every bound client receives this event for the group; any group objects that client holds for it receive a removed event and must be destroyed afterwards.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the name of the dissolved group

interface.name: treeland_output_mirror_group_v1
interface.description:
Represents one mirroring group: a single source wl_output whose rendered content is duplicated to an ordered list of mirror wl_outputs. The group is created empty by treeland_output_mirror_manager_v1.create_group, or handed to an observing client by the manager group_added event.
Object model. The group keeps two disjoint sets of outputs: a source (zero or one) and an ordered list of mirrors (zero or more). An output may belong to at most one group; an output that is already the source or a mirror of another group is rejected with the output_in_use error. The client builds the group incrementally with set_source and add_output, in any order. Copy mode is engaged on the affected outputs while the group has both a source and at least one mirror; a group with no source or no mirrors is inert and those outputs behave as normal extension outputs.
Initial state. Immediately after the group object is created, whether by create_group or group_added, the compositor sends the current state on the new object: one source event (with a null output when the group has no source) followed by one output_added event for each mirror in list order. Subsequent state changes are reported by further source, output_added, and output_removed events.
Multiple objects per group. Several group objects may be bound to the same underlying group, for example one from create_group and others from group_added to observing clients. All of them observe the same state and receive the same change events. Destroying one group object only releases that client's handle; it does not dissolve the group or affect other handles.
Dissolving a group. To tear down copy mode and remove the group, a client sends the dissolve request. The compositor exits copy mode, emits a removed event to every group object bound to this group and a group_removed event on the manager, and the group no longer exists. After the removed event the object is inert; the only valid request on it is destroy, and any other request is rejected with the already_dissolved error.
Hardware removal. When a member output is unplugged or disabled the compositor updates the group automatically. If a mirror is removed the compositor emits output_removed for it. If the source is removed and one or more mirrors remain, the first remaining mirror becomes the new source: the compositor emits output_removed for that output (it leaves the mirror set) followed by a source event for it. If the source is removed and no mirrors remain, the compositor emits a source event with a null output.

enum.name: error
enum.description: Raised as fatal protocol errors on the group object.

entry.name: invalid_output
entry.summary: the provided output is null, disabled, destroyed, or not a recognized enabled wl_output

entry.name: duplicate_output
entry.summary: the output is already the source or a mirror of this group

entry.name: output_in_use
entry.summary: the output is the source or a mirror of another mirror group

entry.name: not_in_group
entry.summary: the output is not a member of this group

entry.name: already_dissolved
entry.summary: the group has been dissolved; only destroy may be sent

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy this treeland_output_mirror_group_v1 object and release the client's handle on the group. The group itself is not affected: copy mode continues, other handles remain valid, and the compositor does not emit group_removed. The client uses the dissolve request to tear down the group as a whole.
It is safe to destroy a group object that has already received the removed event.

request.name: set_source
request.description:
Set the given output as the source of the group, replacing any current source. The previous source, if any, is removed from the group and becomes a normal extension output again.
The output must be a valid, enabled wl_output that is not already a member of this or another group. A null, disabled, or destroyed output is rejected with the invalid_output error. An output that is already the source or a mirror of this group is rejected with the duplicate_output error; to promote a current mirror to the source, first remove it with remove_output and then set it with set_source. An output that belongs to another group is rejected with the output_in_use error.
If the group already has mirrors, setting the source engages or updates copy mode immediately. The compositor confirms the new source by emitting a source event.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the output to designate as the source

request.name: add_output
request.description:
Append the given output to the end of the group's mirror list. The output must be a valid, enabled wl_output that is not already a member of this or another group. A null, disabled, or destroyed output is rejected with the invalid_output error. An output already in this group is rejected with the duplicate_output error. An output in another group is rejected with the output_in_use error.
If the group already has a source, adding a mirror engages or extends copy mode immediately. The compositor confirms by emitting an output_added event. Sources and mirrors may be set in any order; copy mode engages once both are present.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the output to add as a mirror

request.name: remove_output
request.description:
Remove the given output from the group. The output must be a current member of this group; otherwise the compositor raises the not_in_group error.
If the output is a mirror, the compositor emits an output_removed event for it. If the group then has a source but no mirrors, copy mode exits while the source remains set.
If the output is the source, the source is cleared and the compositor emits a source event with a null output; the mirrors are unchanged and copy mode exits. This client-driven removal does not auto-select a successor; to promote a mirror, call set_source on it afterwards. Hardware-driven removal of the source, by contrast, does auto-select a successor as described in the interface description.

request.name: dissolve

description.summary: dissolve the group and exit copy mode

request.description:
Tear down the group: exit copy mode, remove the group from the manager, and release the affected outputs. The compositor emits a removed event to every group object bound to this group and a group_removed event on the manager to every bound client.
After the removed event the group object is inert; the only request the client may send on it is destroy. Any other request is rejected with the already_dissolved error. If the group was already dissolved, sending dissolve again is also rejected with already_dissolved.

event.name: source

description.summary: current source output of the group

event.description: Reports the current source output of the group. It is emitted once immediately after the group object is created, with a null output when the group has no source, and again whenever the source changes: because a client called set_source or removed the source, or because the source output was unplugged or disabled and a successor was selected or none remained.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the current source output, or null when the group has no source

event.name: output_added
event.description: Reports that an output was appended to the mirror list. It is emitted once for each existing mirror, in list order, immediately after the group object is created, and again whenever a client adds a mirror with add_output.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the mirror output that was added

event.name: output_removed
event.description: Reports that an output left the mirror list. It is emitted when a client removes a mirror with remove_output, when a mirror output is unplugged or disabled, or when a mirror is promoted to the source because the previous source was removed and a successor had to be selected.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the mirror output that was removed

event.name: removed
event.description: Emitted to every group object bound to the group when the group is dissolved, whether because a client sent the dissolve request or because the compositor removed the group as a whole. After this event the object is inert and the client must destroy it. No further state events are emitted on the object.
